answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is quadratic stake voting with slashable identity bonds. Each agent locks an opal bond and receives votes equal to the square root of its stake, so splitting a fortune across many fake wallets never multiplies influence; it only burns fees. A signed cipher commitment ties every persona back to one funding key, letting observers cluster a comet swarm of fresh accounts as a single actor and slash the shared bond. Doubling fake identities thus costs roughly twice the locked capital while adding far less than twice the votes.
